transcript: yesterday I saw the national tour of “What the Constitution Means to Me” presented by Broadeay in Chicago I regretted missing the show’s run on Broadway and was so happy when it was filmed and released on Amazon prime a year ago Heidi Schreck’s deeply personal story explores her unique connection to the U.S. Constitution is a teenager where she won scholarship money talking about and debating this 234 year old document. It then pivots to an expiration of what Heidi — now a 45 year old woman — thinks and feels about our Constitution calling attention to how it blatantly pushes women and minorities to the margins It’s both a memory play and political theater with a final act debate thrown into the mix. In this tour, “Heidi” is played by Cassie Beck a very fine performer who manages to overcome the odd magic trick of being both “Heidi” and herself — a working actress cast on the role of Heidi. The night I saw the show, Emmilyn Toffler, who introduces himself as a 17 year old trans man, served as Heidi/Cassie’s debate partner which challenged the audience with the ultimate question of whether we should abolish or keep the constitution. You’ll leave the theater conflicted, hopeful angry, energized and with your own pocket size copy of the Constitution. It plays through Nov. 7th Chicago with multiple cities through early 2022. check out ConstitutionBroadway.com to learn more.
